comment: Artificial intelligence is treated as a cross-cutting consideration. In practice it is becoming a distinct layer with its own components and governance requirements - model registries, provenance and audit of training data, monitoring of deployed models, allocation of liability - none of which map cleanly onto the present two-layer structure.

public.text: Artificial intelligence is treated as a cross-cutting consideration. In practice it is becoming a distinct layer with its own components and governance requirements - model registries, provenance and audit of training data, monitoring of deployed models, allocation of liability - none of which map cleanly onto the present two-layer structure.
public.suggestedRevision: Consider describing AI as a distinct architectural layer resting on the shared data foundation, with its own governance requirements, rather than only as a cross-cutting consideration. Include the requirement that machine-generated content in a health record be labelled as such and remain distinguishable from human-authored content, which is a precondition both for clinical safety and for later training, and which aligns with transparency obligations in the EU AI Act.
